handbookNote: Delaware Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Delaware Real Estate Commission (DREC) (Candidate Handbook #090800, January 2026). Delaware has THREE license tiers -- Salesperson, Associate Broker, and Broker -- but only two exam products: Associate Broker and Broker sit the SAME broker-level exam, diverging only via post-exam management-authority verification under 24 Del. C. Section 2907(d). National/General portion: 80 scored items + 5 unscored pretest, 150 minutes. Delaware State portion: 50 scored items (vs. 40 for Salesperson, Broker gets an additional 10-item Broker-only section) + 10 unscored pretest, 90 minutes. Single combined 4-hour sitting, flat $88 fee (no per-portion fee split like NH/HI's PSI model). Passing score is a SCALED score of 70 (0-100 scale, NOT raw percent-correct), National and State scored/passed INDEPENDENTLY, max 3 attempts per portion before the pre-licensing course must be redone. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=130, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=70, min_correct=91 (round(130*0.70)), same scaled-score convention as UT/NV/KS/ID/NE/WV/WY/AK/MT/RI in this campaign. NATIONAL/GENERAL PORTION (80 items, 8 sections) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas/Idaho/Nebraska/West Virginia/Montana/Rhode Island/Wyoming/Alaska -- Delaware's own Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections). DELAWARE STATE PORTION (50 items, real Broker item counts): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission (4, incl. the real 9-member Commission composition -- 3 brokers by county/1 associate broker/1 salesperson plus 4 public members -- and the real Guaranty Fund cap of $50,000 per claim/transaction under 24 Del. C. Section 2922, corrected from a stale $25,000 figure found in outdated secondary sources), Licensing Requirements (3, incl. the real 5-year/3-active-year/30-transaction broker prerequisite, 99-hour pre-licensing course, and 21-hour biennial CE requirement across seven 3-hour modules), Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees (17, largest section -- Delaware's real Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report and separate Exemption Property Certification form (6 Del. C. Ch. 25), a real radon disclosure statute (24 Del. C. Section 2572A), a distinctively strong Psychologically Impacted Properties non-disclosure rule that affirmatively FORBIDS disclosing HIV/AIDS status even on direct request (24 Del. C. Section 2927), Delaware's presumed-dual-agency default for 1-4 family residential transactions (24 Del. C. Section 2933), and the real Rule 14 Voluntary Treatment Option -- a cross-board impaired/chemically-dependent-licensee program, not a general consumer dispute process as might be assumed from the name), Additional State Topics (16, incl. the Delaware Uniform Common Interest Ownership Act, Delaware's genuinely high combined Realty Transfer Tax -- roughly 4% in New Castle County vs 3.5% in Kent/Sussex County, with a real first-time-homebuyer 1/2% reduction -- the Clear Zone Safety Law's 10-ft sign setback, Delaware's pure RACE recording statute (24 Del. C. Section 153, not race-notice), and confirmation that Delaware's UETA does NOT exclude real estate contracts from e-signature validity), and Broker Only (10, no Salesperson equivalent -- escrow account rules under Section 2923 (72-hour deposit deadline), the real Delaware Foreclosure Consultants Act, New Home Buyer Protection Act escrow-for-unfinished-work rules, the Commercial Broker's Lien Act, and Mortgage Loan Modification Services Act licensee exemption). Governing law: Delaware Code Title 24, Chapter 29 (Real Estate Services, Brokers, Associate Brokers and Salespersons) and 24 Del. Admin. Code Section 2900. This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
